TAG Heuer · ref. WBP5110.BA0013

Aquaracer

Dive · 27–45mm · 200–1000m · automatic · 2000–2004

The Aquaracer is TAG Heuer's family of robust and versatile dive watches, defined by its six signature features: a unidirectional rotating bezel, a screw-down crown, water resistance of at least 200 meters, luminous markings, a sapphire crystal, and a double safety clasp. Its design often includes a 12-sided bezel and a horizontally-striped dial.

The story

The Aquaracer's lineage began with the Heuer 2000 series in 1982, a versatile sports watch collection that was an evolution of the brand's first dive watches from the late 1970s. The "Aquaracer" name was officially introduced in 2004, rebranding the 2000 series and upgrading the water resistance from 200m to 300m. Subsequent generations saw significant evolution, including the introduction of a more angular 500m-rated model in 2009, the use of ceramic bezels from 2012, and a major redesign in 2021 with the "Professional 300" line. The family has consistently offered both quartz and automatic movements, including the popular Calibre 5, and has expanded to include chronographs, GMTs, and innovative Solargraph technology.
